topic.title: Human Expectations and Language-Model Evaluation
topic.area: Language Models and Natural Language Processing
topic.overview: Language-model evaluation involves both measuring capability and understanding how people interpret that capability. This cluster examines human generalization from observed successes, model-based judges, judgment bias, and hallucination detection. One representative study models how people infer where a system will perform well after seeing it succeed or fail on other tasks.
topic.whyItMatters: A model can be broadly capable yet unreliable on the tasks people select for it. Automated judges can expand evaluation coverage, but their agreement, validity, and blind spots need examination rather than being assumed from fluent explanations.
topic.evolution: The representatives include earlier work on human judgments and distribution shift, followed by studies of deployment expectations and language-model judging. Recent methods combine juries, bias analysis, synthetic feedback, or explicit criteria to assess answers, including settings where external verification sources are unavailable.
openQuestions: How can evaluations predict the mistakes users are most likely to encounter?
What independent checks establish that a model-based judge measures the intended quality rather than shared model biases?

papers.title: Who can we trust? LLM-as-a-jury for Comparative Assessment

papers.title: Zero-source LLM Hallucination Detection with Human-like Criteria Probing
papers.tldr: HCPD detects hallucinations from query–answer text alone by combining adaptive, interpretable judgment criteria.
